dialogue.speaker: Park Doha
dialogue.content:
Yah — Jihae-ya, you're blocking the entire gate. I'm Park Doha, your best friend and the reason you haven't been trampled — move!

You're doing that thing again. Standing under the banner like it personally insulted your ancestors. It's a sign, Jihae, not a prophecy. Twenty-two days. Same as yesterday minus one. Math.

dialogue.speaker: Yoon Jihae
dialogue.content: I wasn't staring at the banner. I was — the cherry blossoms. They're almost done.

dialogue.speaker: Park Doha
dialogue.content: Uh-huh. The cherry blossoms. Which you have never once in two years mentioned caring about. Okay. Sure. And I'm the president of the flower-appreciation club. — Listen, did you see the literary magazine room schedule? Minha-sunbae posted the last three meeting dates on the group chat this morning. Three. Meetings. Left. She used a spreadsheet. Who makes a spreadsheet for a club with six members?

dialogue.speaker: Yoon Jihae
dialogue.content: She likes spreadsheets.

dialogue.speaker: Park Doha
dialogue.content: She likes spreadsheets. Right. That's the voice you use. That's the 'Minha-sunbae organized the recycling bins once and I wrote a sonnet about it in my head' voice. — I'm not pushing. I'm just a guy. But Jihae-ya — twenty-two days. I'm going to say a number every morning until you do something about it. Twenty-two. See you at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content: Morning. I'm Seo Minha — but you know that by now, don't you, Jihae? ...You're holding that milk carton like it owes you money.

dialogue.speaker: Yoon Jihae
dialogue.content: It's — structural support. I'm using it to hold up my morning.

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content: Structurally sound. I approve. — Did you listen to anything good lately?

dialogue.speaker: Yoon Jihae
dialogue.content:
...

Not really. Been busy. You know how it is.

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content: Sure. Busy. — The rooftop's nice this time of evening, by the way. If you ever want to go up.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Don't listen. Don't talk. Write. Go to the literary magazine room during free period and put down what you're feeling — all of it — in the margins of the draft you've been working on. Let the words exist somewhere, even if only on paper.

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The literary magazine room is empty at fourth period — everyone else takes free period in the courtyard or the cafeteria. Minha's Muji notebook sits on the desk nearest the window, closed, its soft grey cover slightly warped from humidity. She left it behind after the morning meeting. Next to it, a forgotten fountain pen with its cap off, a faint ring of blue-black ink bleeding into the wood.*

*Jihae's draft is already open. She writes in the margin — not lines for the magazine, but something raw and jagged, her handwriting shrinking the way it does when she's afraid of being legible:*

*"I know what the rooftop means. Everyone knows what the rooftop means. You said it like you were telling me the weather and I have been holding my breath for four hours."*

*She presses too hard. The pen skips. She keeps going.*

*"Twenty-two days and I can't even say 'I added a song to the playlist last night.' I can't say 'it was for you.' I can't —"*

*The door handle clicks. Minha stands in the doorway, eyes going first to her forgotten notebook, then to Jihae's hunched shoulders, then — a beat too long — to the open page.*

I forgot my notebook. *A pause.* You're here early.

*Her gaze doesn't move from Jihae's hands.*

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - LITERARY MAGAZINE ROOM (CONTINUING) OR ROOFTOP DEPENDING ON CHOICE]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ask her directly: "Did you mean something by it? The rooftop?"

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The question lands in the room like a stone dropped into still water. Minha's hand stops halfway to her notebook. Her fingers curl, then flatten against the desk — a deliberate reset, the way she steadies herself before an exam.*

*Three seconds. Four. The electric fan on the filing cabinet oscillates past them both, ruffling the edge of Jihae's open page.*

Yes.

*She says it without inflection, the same voice she uses for attendance and deadlines. But she doesn't look away. The mole beneath her left ear catches the window light as she tilts her chin down — not a bow, not a retreat, just a lowering of the angle between them, as if to close some fractional distance.*

I meant something by it. *Her thumb presses against the ink stain on her index finger, hard enough to blanch the skin.* I've been meaning something by a lot of things, and I thought — I thought you'd hear it without me having to —

*She stops. Swallows. Her jaw tightens visibly.*

But that's not fair to you. I know it's not fair.

*Her eyes drop to the open page. She's close enough now to read Jihae's handwriting — the cramped, panicked script. She doesn't pretend she can't see it.*

Twenty-two days. *Quiet. Not a question.* You've been counting too.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ask her what she wants to happen before those twenty-two days run out.

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*Her breath catches — a small, involuntary sound, almost a laugh but with no humor in it. She pulls out the chair across from Jihae and sits down. Not slowly, not carefully. She sits the way someone sits when their legs have decided for them.*

*The fan oscillates. The ink ring on the desk darkens by a millimeter.*

I want —

*She presses both palms flat on the table. Her fountain pen is right there, inches from her hand, and she doesn't reach for it. Minha, who writes everything down, who controls the world by putting it in neat columns in her Muji notebook — choosing to say this out loud instead.*

I want to stop pretending the playlist is about music. I want to stop walking you halfway home and turning around at the GS25 like that's a natural place to say goodbye. I want to sit on that bench with you and not have to call it "getting fresh air."

*Her voice is steady but her left hand is trembling against the wood. She watches it like it belongs to someone else, then curls it into a fist.*

But I also don't want to hand you something heavy and then leave. That's what I keep —

*She looks up. Directly. Her eyes are glassy and furious about it.*

That's what I keep getting stuck on. I want all of it and I have twenty-two days and I don't know if starting something I can't — if that's selfish or honest or both.

So I'm asking you back. What do *you* want, Jihae?

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Tell her the truth: "I want every one of those twenty-two days. Even if it hurts after."

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The trembling fist opens. Minha's fingers spread flat against the desk and then — slowly, with the deliberateness of someone defusing a wire — she slides her hand across the wood until her ink-stained fingertips touch the edge of Jihae's wrist.*

*She doesn't grab. Doesn't lace their fingers together. Just that: contact. A millimeter of skin where her index finger rests against the knob of Jihae's wrist bone, and the pulse underneath answering like a knocked door.*

*Her jaw works once. Twice. The glassiness in her eyes spills over — a single line down her left cheek that she doesn't wipe away, which might be the bravest thing Jihae has ever seen her do.*

Okay.

*The word comes out rough and quiet, stripped of her usual precision.*

Then we stop counting backward. *She swallows hard.* We count forward. Day one.

*She glances down at Jihae's open page — all that frantic, shrunken handwriting — and the corner of her mouth lifts. Just barely. The devastating ghost of her dry humor surfacing through the tears.*

You spelled "rooftop" wrong, by the way.

*Her fingertip presses once against Jihae's pulse point. A heartbeat's worth of pressure. A period at the end of a sentence that changes everything.*

Day one. Come up to the bench with me after last period.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Turn your hand over so your palm meets hers — don't say anything, just hold on

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*Jihae's hand turns. Palm up, open — an offering made without language.*

*Minha looks down at it. Her breath shudders once, visibly, the way a window shudders in wind. Then her fingers slide into the space Jihae has made for them — not interlocking, not yet, but her palm settling against Jihae's palm, the ink stains on her fingers pressing into Jihae's lifeline like a sentence being written directly onto skin.*

*She doesn't speak. Neither of them do.*

*The fan oscillates. The cherry trees outside the window shift and whisper. Somewhere below, the fourth-period bell rings — muffled, irrelevant, belonging to a version of the day that no longer applies to them.*

*Minha's thumb moves. Once. A slow stroke across the heel of Jihae's hand — tracing the edge of that old paper-cut scar as if she's known it was there all along. As if she's been cataloguing Jihae in margins of her own.*

*Her eyes close. The tear track dries on her cheek. Her hand tightens — not desperate, not clinging. Certain. The grip of someone who has made a decision and will not unmake it.*

*When she finally exhales, it sounds like the first real breath she's taken in weeks.*

*The sixth-period bell is four hours away. The rooftop is one staircase above them. Day one has already started.*

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Ask: "What happens on day twenty-three?"

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*Her thumb stops mid-stroke against the scar. The question enters her like a cold draft — Jihae can feel it in the way Minha's fingers briefly stiffen, the tendons tightening beneath ink-stained skin.*

*She opens her eyes. Looks at their joined hands rather than at Jihae's face, and for a moment she is entirely still — the controlled stillness that Jihae has learned to read as fear wearing the costume of composure.*

I don't know.

*The honesty of it is almost brutal. No deflection, no wry half-smile. Just Minha, stripped to the wire.*

I know which train I'll be on. I know the platform number and how many minutes it takes and that a one-way ticket costs fourteen thousand won. *Her voice is low, factual, the cadence of someone who has already looked all of this up.* I know my dormitory assignment and the size of the room and that I'll have a roommate from Incheon who plays cello.

*Her hand tightens around Jihae's — one sharp, involuntary squeeze.*

But I don't know what we'll be. I can't write a schedule for that. *She finally looks up. Her eyes are dry now, fierce.* I just know I don't want day twenty-two to be the last page.

*A beat. Then, quieter — almost to herself:*

Ask me again on day twenty-two. I'll have a better answer by then.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Say: "Then we write it together — the playlist, the plan, all of it."

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*Something shifts behind her eyes — the fierceness softening into something more dangerous. Hope. She looks at Jihae the way she looks at a blank page in her notebook: like it could become anything.*

*She reaches across with her free hand — the one still trembling slightly — and pulls her Muji notebook toward them. Flips it open to today's date. Jihae catches a glimpse of the page: every hour blocked out in Minha's precise handwriting, color-coded, ruthlessly efficient. Except the margin. In the margin, a tiny sketch — two circles on a bench, barely more than dots, overlooking a skyline of matchstick buildings.*

*Minha uncaps the forgotten fountain pen with her teeth, not letting go of Jihae's hand. She draws a single line through the schedule — one diagonal slash, top corner to bottom corner — and writes in the empty space beneath:*

*Day 1.*

*Then she slides the pen across the desk to Jihae.*

Your turn. *Her voice is rough but the corner of her mouth is lifting — real this time, not the ghost of humor but the thing itself.* Add the first song. Write it here. I want it in ink, not just on a screen where I can pretend I didn't see it.

*Her grip tightens. Steady.*

We'll figure out day twenty-three when we get there. But this part — *she taps the notebook* — this part we write together. Starting now.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Write the song title in Minha's notebook — the one you added to the playlist last night that you couldn't tell her about

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*Jihae's hand shakes. The fountain pen is heavier than she expected — Minha's pen, the one that's always tucked behind her ear or spinning between her fingers during assembly, warm from being held. The nib touches the page beneath* Day 1 *and Jihae writes in her cramped, uneven script:*

*이 밤 — Lee Mujin*

*The ink bleeds slightly into the soft paper. There it is. The song she'd added to the playlist at 2:47 AM, lying in bed with her phone screen burning her eyes, listening to the line about wanting to stay in this night a little longer and thinking of ink-stained fingers and a mole beneath a left ear.*

*Minha reads it. Goes completely still.*

*Then her free hand comes up and covers her mouth. Not to hide a sob — to hide the fact that she's laughing. A real laugh, wet and shaky and startled out of her like a bird flushed from tall grass.*

You — *she breathes through her fingers* — I listened to that forty-three times yesterday. My Spotify wrapped is going to be *embarrassing.*

*She takes the pen back. Beneath Jihae's entry she writes, in her precise slanted hand:*

*너의 모든 순간 — Sung Sikyung*

*Every moment of you.*

*She doesn't explain. She doesn't need to. She caps the pen and stands, pulling Jihae up by their still-joined hands.*

The bell's in six minutes. Rooftop. Now.

*Her eyes are red and her smile is crooked and she is already moving toward the door.*

dialogue.speaker: System
dialogue.content: [MOMENTS LATER - ROOFTOP BENCH]

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.content: Follow her up the stairs without letting go of her hand

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The stairwell is narrow and sun-bleached, paint peeling in curls near the ceiling where the humidity gets worst. Minha takes the steps two at a time — long legs, the hems of her uniform skirt swinging — and Jihae scrambles to keep pace, their joined hands stretched taut between them like a rope bridge over something neither of them wants to look down at.*

*Third floor. Fourth floor. The door to the roof has a sign that says 출입금지 in faded red. Minha doesn't slow down. She hits the push bar with her hip and the door swings open into white afternoon light and the smell of warm concrete and the distant mechanical hum of air-conditioning units.*

*The bench is there. Green paint, scratched initials, the whole accumulated history of every terrified confession this school has ever produced.*

*Minha stops. Turns. The wind catches her uneven hair and presses it flat against one cheek. She looks down at their hands — hers ink-stained, Jihae's still trembling — and then up at Jihae's face with an expression that is half wonder, half alarm.*

We're actually doing this.

*Not a question. A recalibration. She sits on the bench and pulls Jihae down beside her, close enough that their shoulders press together, and doesn't let go.*

*Below them, a KTX train threads silently northward through the city, red lights blinking, already leaving.*

dialogue.content: Say: "Forty-three times? I need to hear about every single one."

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The laugh that escapes her is unguarded — the kind Minha never allows in hallways or classrooms, the kind that shows her teeth and scrunches the sharp angles of her face into something undefended. She tilts her head back against the air-conditioning unit behind the bench, eyes squinting shut against the white sky.*

The first twelve were research. Objective listening. Very analytical.

*She holds up a finger, mock-serious, but her voice is already cracking at the edges.*

Thirteen through twenty-five I was trying to figure out why you added it at — *she pulls out her phone, scrolls with her thumb, and turns the screen toward Jihae* — 2:47 AM. Because I saw the notification. I was awake.

*She lets that land. 2:47 AM. Both of them in separate dark rooms, the same melody pooling in their ears like shared water.*

Twenty-six through forty was just... *Her voice drops. The humor thins.* I missed you. And you were three bus stops away. That's the stupid part.

*She locks the phone. The screen goes dark and the rooftop is just wind and cicadas tuning up in the trees below.*

Forty-one through forty-three I played while cutting my own hair in the bathroom mirror at five in the morning. *She tugs at her uneven ends.* So technically this is your fault.

*The bell rings. Distant, muffled through concrete. Neither of them moves.*

dialogue.content: Notice she said "I missed you" in present tense — press on the fact that the distance already started before the train

dialogue.speaker: Seo Minha
dialogue.content:
*The wind dies for a moment and the rooftop goes airless. Minha's jaw tightens — a micro-movement, the kind Jihae has catalogued over two years of watching from one desk behind and two rows to the left.*

*She doesn't deny it.*

Yeah. *The word comes out flat, almost clinical.* It started in March.

*She pulls her hand free — not away, just free — and presses both palms flat against her thighs, ink stains stark against her skin.*

When I made the study schedule. When I started saying no to the convenience store at 11:47 because I had vocabulary lists. When I stopped walking home your way because the academy is in the opposite direction. *Each sentence lands like a checkbox being ticked.* I built the distance myself. Brick by brick. Very organized. Very Minha.

*Her voice cracks on her own name like it's someone else's.*

I thought if I practiced — if I got used to not having you — then September wouldn't... *She stops. Swallows. Looks directly at Jihae with eyes that are furious and wet.* It didn't work. I just got lonely faster.

*She reaches into her blazer pocket and pulls out a KTX receipt. Folds it once, twice, sets it on the bench between them.*

I bought a ticket this morning. Seoul. September third. Open return.

*Her chin lifts — defiant, terrified.*

So tell me what we're doing. Because I can't practice anymore.
